note: Durvalumab reached HCC patients on no HCC model (it does not bind mouse PD-L1; its filed in-vivo work was human-T-cell co-implant xenografts and CT26 mice with a surrogate), yet the academic surrogate mouse HCC models, the monkey toxicology and the PD-L1-knockout liver phenotype all agreed in direction with HIMALAYA; benmelstobart and sugemalimab have HCC patient data but no model comparison.
label: HCC (anti-PD-L1)

engagement.judgement: Opening entry. Durvalumab does not bind mouse PD-L1 (FDA pharmacology review 2017), so the only product-dosed PD system was this human-cell assay, which the review lists as study ONC4736-0020 (3 ug/mL gave 90% of maximal proliferation in all eight donors). Dated to first publication; the filed study predates it.
engagement.model: Primary human T-cell activation assay (proliferation, IFN-gamma) with durvalumab; filed as ONC4736-0020
engagement.note: Durvalumab restored primary human T-cell activation in vitro, 90% of maximal response at 3 ug/mL per FDA; no HCC patient had been dosed.
engagement.short: In-vitro T-cell activation, no patients yet
engagement.quote: In vitro assays demonstrate that MEDI4736 is a potent antagonist of PD-L1 function, blocking interaction with PD-1 and CD80 to overcome inhibition of primary human T-cell activation.

engagement.magnitude_basis: T-cell proliferation in vitro vs early expansion of proliferating CD8+ lymphocytes in HCC patients' blood
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Kelley 2021. The abstract says the expansion was associated with response across arms but gives the durvalumab-monotherapy magnitude only relative to T300+D, where tremelimumab drove the largest rise.
engagement.judgement: Pairing is mine: the assay's readout (T-cell proliferation) against proliferating CD8+ lymphocytes in HCC patients on durvalumab 1500 mg Q4W. Partial and direction only because the biggest expansion needed tremelimumab, a non-member. The FDA clinical pharmacology review's sPD-L1 suppression (complete at >=0.3 mg/kg Q2W) is a direct-tier readout but was measured in non-HCC patients of Study 1108 and was not predicted by any model, so it is noted, not scored.
engagement.model: Primary human T-cell activation assay (proliferation, IFN-gamma) with durvalumab; filed as ONC4736-0020
engagement.note: Study 22: early CD8+ lymphocyte expansion tracked response across arms, including durvalumab alone (ORR 10.6%); largest with the tremelimumab priming dose.
engagement.short: CD8+ proliferation rose in dosed HCC patients
engagement.quote: An early expansion of CD8+ lymphocytes was associated with response across arms, with highest proliferating CD8+ lymphocyte levels occurring in the T300 + D arm.
engagement.reason: T-cell proliferation readout moved in patients

dose.judgement: The model's dose statement is a tolerability margin (13-week NOAEL = highest dose, 200/100 mg/kg/week), not an efficacy exposure: durvalumab does not bind mouse PD-L1, and the clinical regimen was set from sPD-L1 suppression in Study 1108 patients plus the in-vitro 3 ug/mL figure. Untested here because the tile scores HCC patients only; the first HCC trial (Study 22, NCT02519348) had not reported.
dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey 4-week and 13-week GLP repeat-dose toxicology of durvalumab (up to 200/100 mg/kg/week)
dose.note: Monkey NOAEL exposure sat 19.7-fold above the AUC at 10 mg/kg Q2W; the regimen came from patient sPD-L1 saturation; no HCC patient dosed.
dose.short: Monkey margin 19.7x; HCC not yet dosed
dose.quote: The exposures in the monkey GLP studies were up to 19.7-fold higher than the clinical AUC of 1773.2 μg*hr/mL (at the clinically recommended dose of 10 mg/kg every two weeks).

dose.magnitude_basis: monkey 13-week NOAEL exposure vs patient AUC at 10 mg/kg Q2W (the 1500 mg Q4W equivalent): 19.7-fold margin
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Abou-Alfa 2022. The 1500 mg Q4W regimen is AstraZeneca's flat-dose equivalent of 10 mg/kg Q2W; I did not re-derive the HCC AUC.
dose.judgement: Reached-and-worked rule on the member drug's own gate: durvalumab monotherapy met its pre-specified non-inferiority objective and the STRIDE arm (durvalumab plus tremelimumab) met the primary OS endpoint. Decision 16: the monkey stated a tolerated exposure 19.7x the clinical AUC and HCC patients took the full regimen with fewer grade 3/4 events than sorafenib, so margin_stated true. EMERALD-1 (Sangro 2025) dosed the same regimen with TACE; its primary (durvalumab plus bevacizumab) was met and the durvalumab-alone PFS comparison was a secondary, so it does not turn this cell.
dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey 4-week and 13-week GLP repeat-dose toxicology of durvalumab (up to 200/100 mg/kg/week)
dose.note: HIMALAYA: durvalumab 1500 mg Q4W reached in 389 HCC patients, monotherapy non-inferior to sorafenib (OS HR 0.86); grade 3/4 TEAEs 37.1% vs 52.4% on sorafenib.
dose.quote: Overall survival with durvalumab monotherapy was noninferior to sorafenib (hazard ratio, 0.86; 95.67% CI, 0.73 to 1.03; noninferiority margin, 1.08).

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the single-agent anti-PD-L1 arm, if run, is not described in the abstract.
efficacy.judgement: Earliest in-vivo anti-PD-L1 antibody in a mouse HCC model that Europe PMC returned (two searches, 2012-2021). Durvalumab does not bind mouse PD-L1, so every mouse HCC datum for this class is a rat anti-mouse surrogate (product_in_model false); no sponsor filed an HCC model (the 2017 BLA's in-vivo work was A375/HPAC co-implant xenografts and CT26 colorectal mice). One track pools the later syngeneic and orthotopic surrogate studies (e.g. Zhu 2019 Gut, OPN-high Hepa1-6) because the system and the prediction, that anti-PD-L1 alone is modest and works in combination, are the same.
efficacy.model: Transgenic c-myc/OVA multifocal mouse HCC dosed with rat anti-mouse PD-L1 (B7-H1) antibody in combination with anti-CD137 and anti-OX40
efficacy.note: Anti-PD-L1 as part of a triple immunostimulatory combination extended survival of mice with multifocal HCC; no HCC patient had received an anti-PD-L1.
efficacy.short: Surrogate anti-PD-L1 combo extends mouse survival
efficacy.quote: The triple combination of ISmAbs extended survival of mice bearing hepatocellular carcinomas in a CD8-dependent fashion and synergized with adoptive T-cell therapy using activated OVA-specific TCR-transgenic OT-1 and OT-2 lymphocytes.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: mouse survival extension with anti-PD-L1 in combination vs HIMALAYA OS: STRIDE HR 0.78, durvalumab alone non-inferior (HR 0.86)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of both sides. The mouse prediction is for anti-PD-L1 within an immunostimulatory combination; the trial's primary arm combines durvalumab with tremelimumab (a non-member), and the member-only arm met a non-inferiority secondary objective.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me; the trial does not cite the mouse work. Same, direction only, at low confidence: the mouse HCC models show anti-PD-L1 activity mainly in combination, and in patients the combination arm met the primary endpoint while durvalumab alone was non-inferior, not superior, to sorafenib (ORR 10.6% in Study 22). Not contra because no member failed a primary endpoint in HCC: EMERALD-1's primary (TACE plus durvalumab plus bevacizumab) was met and its durvalumab-alone PFS arm was a secondary (results read from memory, not verified at full text). Pfister 2021's NASH-HCC mouse comparison is excluded: its mice got anti-PD-1 and its pooled trials used atezolizumab, nivolumab and pembrolizumab, none a member. Benmelstobart (TQB2450) has HCC patient data (phase 1b with AL2846, ORR 0/15 in ICI-refractory HCC, Cancer 2024, doi 10.1002/cncr.35377; several phase 2s and a phase 3 with ablation, NCT04665609, status unknown) and sugemalimab a phase 1b/2 with fisogatinib (NCT04194801, results posted 2023-02-06); I found no model comparison for either, so neither scores.

patient_trials.quote: We aimed to assess whether adding durvalumab, with or without bevacizumab, might improve progression-free survival.

efficacy.model: Transgenic c-myc/OVA multifocal mouse HCC dosed with rat anti-mouse PD-L1 (B7-H1) antibody in combination with anti-CD137 and anti-OX40
efficacy.note: HIMALAYA: durvalumab plus one tremelimumab dose beat sorafenib on OS (HR 0.78); durvalumab alone was non-inferior (HR 0.86), as the combination-dependent mouse data pointed.
efficacy.quote: STRIDE significantly improved overall survival versus sorafenib. Durvalumab monotherapy was noninferior to sorafenib for patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma.

efficacy.model: Human T-cell co-implant xenograft: PD-L1+ human A375 melanoma or HPAC pancreatic cells mixed with alloreactive human CD4+/CD8+ T cells in NOD-SCID mice, dosed with MEDI4736 (durvalumab); filed as ONC4736-0006
efficacy.confidence_note: Proxy date: the FDA review gives the study report date (7 February 2012, non-GLP, MedImmune Cambridge); the review itself is dated 2017. Read from the reviewer's text, not the applicant's report.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry for the system durvalumab's BLA actually relied on for efficacy: the review's only in-vivo pharmacology study with the product, ONC4736-0006 (the checker's 'ONC4736-0019' is the CT26 surrogate dose-level study, tracked separately). Melanoma and pancreatic lines in NOD-SCID mice, so cross_indication; no HCC line was used. Kept apart from the CT26 track: different antibody (the product, not a surrogate), different immune system (transplanted human T cells) and a product-specific prediction (durvalumab's own activity needs T cells).
efficacy.note: MEDI4736 cut HPAC and A375 growth up to 74% and 95% only with co-implanted human T cells; no HCC patient yet dosed.
efficacy.quote: MEDI4736 significantly inhibited growth of HPAC (Fig 5) and A375 (Fig 6) cells by up to 74% and 95%, respectively, as compared to the control group (CAT254).

efficacy.model: Human T-cell co-implant xenograft: PD-L1+ human A375 melanoma or HPAC pancreatic cells mixed with alloreactive human CD4+/CD8+ T cells in NOD-SCID mice, dosed with MEDI4736 (durvalumab); filed as ONC4736-0006
efficacy.magnitude_basis: tumor growth inhibition up to 74% (HPAC) and 95% (A375) with MEDI4736 in co-implant mice vs HIMALAYA durvalumab-monotherapy OS HR 0.86 (non-inferior to sorafenib) and Study 22 confirmed ORR 10.6%

patient_trials.quote: Progression-free survival hazard ratio was 0·77 (95% CI 0·61-0·98; two-sided p=0·032) for durvalumab plus bevacizumab versus placebo, and 0·94 (0·75-1·19; two-sided p=0·64) for durvalumab plus placebo versus placebo.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Abou-Alfa 2022 and Kelley 2021. Cross-indication pairing: melanoma and pancreatic xenografts set against HCC patients; neither trial cites the model.
efficacy.judgement: Pairing is mine. The model's prediction is that durvalumab itself, acting through T cells, slows PD-L1+ human tumors as a single agent; in HCC, durvalumab alone was non-inferior to sorafenib on OS (a pre-specified secondary objective; the trial's primary was STRIDE, with the non-member tremelimumab) and gave confirmed responses in 10.6% of Study 22 patients. Direction agreed, so same at low confidence, matching the draft's existing efficacy call and inheriting the checker's open rule question on combination-arm primaries. EMERALD-1 is recorded, not scored: its primary (durvalumab plus bevacizumab plus TACE, PFS HR 0.77) was met and the durvalumab-plus-TACE comparison (HR 0.94) was a key secondary in a different, embolisation-eligible setting; its final OS (HR 1.10, ESMO GI 2026 abstract) is a key secondary I did not fetch. Not retro: the model (2012) predates every HCC trial.
efficacy.note: HIMALAYA: durvalumab alone non-inferior to sorafenib on OS (HR 0.86); Study 22 ORR 10.6%; single-agent activity the co-implant model foretold, in direction.
efficacy.short: Monotherapy activity held in HCC patients
efficacy.quote: Overall survival with durvalumab monotherapy was noninferior to sorafenib (hazard ratio, 0.86; 95.67% CI, 0.73 to 1.03; noninferiority margin, 1.08).
efficacy.reason: Filed xenograft direction held; HCC unmodelled

efficacy.model: Syngeneic CT26 mouse colorectal carcinoma dosed with a rat anti-mouse PD-L1 surrogate antibody (durvalumab does not bind mouse PD-L1), alone or with oxaliplatin; filed as ONC4736-0018 and ONC4736-0019
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Dated to first publication (epub 2015-05-05); the filed CT26 studies ONC4736-0018 and -0019 appear in the FDA pharmacology review's study table without dates or results, so the system predates 2015 by an unknown margin.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry on the second filed efficacy system: an immunocompetent syngeneic colorectal model dosed with a rat anti-mouse PD-L1 antibody because durvalumab does not bind mouse PD-L1 (product_in_model false). Separate track from the co-implant xenograft: different antibody, different host immune system, and a mechanism-level prediction (PD-L1 blockade alone improves survival, more with oxaliplatin) rather than a product-level one. Also separate from the draft's academic HCC surrogate track (c-myc/OVA transgenic HCC with a triple immunostimulatory combination): different tumor, different prediction (monotherapy).
efficacy.note: Anti-mouse PD-L1 alone prolonged survival of CT26-bearing mice, more with oxaliplatin; filed as ONC4736-0018/-0019; no HCC patient on an anti-PD-L1.
efficacy.short: Surrogate anti-PD-L1 monotherapy prolongs CT26 survival
efficacy.quote: Here, anti-mouse PD-L1 significantly improved survival of mice implanted with CT26 colorectal cancer cells.

efficacy.model: Syngeneic CT26 mouse colorectal carcinoma dosed with a rat anti-mouse PD-L1 surrogate antibody (durvalumab does not bind mouse PD-L1), alone or with oxaliplatin; filed as ONC4736-0018 and ONC4736-0019
efficacy.magnitude_basis: survival benefit of surrogate anti-PD-L1 monotherapy in CT26 mice vs HIMALAYA durvalumab-monotherapy OS HR 0.86 (non-inferior to sorafenib)

patient_trials.quote: Progression-free survival hazard ratio was 0·77 (95% CI 0·61-0·98; two-sided p=0·032) for durvalumab plus bevacizumab versus placebo, and 0·94 (0·75-1·19; two-sided p=0·64) for durvalumab plus placebo versus placebo.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Surrogate antibody in a colorectal, not HCC, model; the trial does not cite the model. The mouse survival magnitude is not in the abstract, so magnitude is direction only.
efficacy.judgement: Pairing is mine. The surrogate predicted single-agent survival benefit from PD-L1 blockade in an immunocompetent host; in HCC, durvalumab alone was non-inferior to sorafenib on OS (secondary non-inferiority objective; the primary was STRIDE with the non-member tremelimumab). Same, direction only, low confidence, matching the draft's existing efficacy call. The 2021 follow-up with effector-function-null murine surrogates of durvalumab and tremelimumab in syngeneic models (PMID 33397194) sits on this track's model side but adds no patient comparison. EMERALD-1's durvalumab-plus-TACE PFS miss (HR 0.94, key secondary) is recorded in patient_trials, not scored.
efficacy.note: HIMALAYA: durvalumab alone non-inferior to sorafenib (OS HR 0.86); the surrogate's monotherapy survival prediction held in direction in HCC patients.
efficacy.short: Surrogate monotherapy direction held in HCC
efficacy.quote: Overall survival with durvalumab monotherapy was noninferior to sorafenib (hazard ratio, 0.86; 95.67% CI, 0.73 to 1.03; noninferiority margin, 1.08).
efficacy.reason: Surrogate CT26 direction held in HCC

safety.judgement: Opening entry on a genetic track kept apart from the monkey: different system, and it predicts an organ (liver) the monkey did not. The FDA review cites PD-L1-knockout mice only for infection susceptibility (Mueller 2010); the hepatitis pairing is mine. Latchman 2004 (PNAS, doi 10.1073/pnas.0307252101) independently showed PD-L1-null mice convert to EAE-susceptible.
safety.model: PD-L1 (B7-H1)-deficient mouse: spontaneous intrahepatic CD8+ T-cell accumulation and accelerated experimental autoimmune hepatitis
safety.note: B7-H1-null mice accumulate CD8+ T cells in the liver and suffer worse autoimmune hepatitis: a standing prediction of immune-mediated liver injury from PD-L1 loss.
safety.quote: Moreover, antigen-driven CD8(+) T cells proliferated normally while apoptotic levels during the contraction phase was selectively impaired in the liver, leading to accelerated hepatocyte damage in experimental autoimmune hepatitis.

safety.magnitude_basis: accelerated autoimmune hepatitis in knockout mice vs immune-mediated hepatitis in 1.1% of durvalumab patients (one fatal)
safety.judgement: Imported from the urothelial-carcinoma BLA population (combined database of several solid tumours). Direction only: a 1.1% incidence against a knockout phenotype that needed an autoimmune-hepatitis challenge. In HCC, HIMALAYA reported immune-mediated events in 16.5% of durvalumab-arm participants (Hepatology 2025) but I could not read the hepatic subset, so no HCC-specific entry is added on this track.
safety.model: PD-L1 (B7-H1)-deficient mouse: spontaneous intrahepatic CD8+ T-cell accumulation and accelerated experimental autoimmune hepatitis
safety.note: Durvalumab label: immune-mediated hepatitis in 16/1414 (1.1%) of the combined safety database, one death; the liver harm the knockout foretold.
safety.quote: Immune-mediated hepatitis occurred in patients receiving IMFINZI.
safety.reason: Knockout liver prediction held in patients

safety.confidence_note: Proxy date: the review gives no study dates I read; the first-in-human trial NCT01693562 was posted 2012-09-26, so the IND-enabling monkey studies were run by then.
safety.judgement: Opening entry, proxy-dated. Rodents were not a relevant species (74% homology, no binding), so the monkey is the class's only product-dosed animal safety system.
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey 4-week and 13-week GLP repeat-dose toxicology of durvalumab (up to 200/100 mg/kg/week)
safety.note: Monkeys, the only binding species, were dosed for up to 13 weeks before the first patient; multi-organ arteritis, infiltrates and thymic atrophy, nothing yet compared.
safety.short: Monkey toxicology filed, no comparison yet
safety.quote: The safety of durvalumab was characterized in a non-GLP dose range-finding study and in GLP 28-day and 13-week toxicology studies in monkeys.

safety.magnitude_basis: immune-mediated rash in one monkey at 200/100 mg/kg/week vs immune-related dermatitis or rash in Study 1108 patients at 10 mg/kg
safety.judgement: Comparison stated by the reviewer, who also called the arteritis/periarteritis and inflammatory infiltrates consistent with PD-L1's role in peripheral tolerance. Partial: the monkey showed the immune-mediated class of harm but not the organs (liver, lung, colon, endocrine) that dominate in patients. Imported from the urothelial-carcinoma BLA; Study 1108 enrolled several solid tumours.
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey 4-week and 13-week GLP repeat-dose toxicology of durvalumab (up to 200/100 mg/kg/week)
safety.note: FDA set the monkey's immune-mediated rash and multi-organ arteritis beside patients' immune-related dermatitis; patients also had hepatitis, pneumonitis and colitis the monkey lacked.
safety.short: Monkey immune lesions matched irAEs, partly
safety.quote: These findings may be attributed to immune-mediated response. In humans, administration of durvalumab at the recommended dose of 10 mg/kg (study #1108,214) resulted in immune-related adverse events (dermatitis or rash).

safety.magnitude_basis: immune-mediated lesions in monkeys vs imAEs in 16.5% of HCC patients on durvalumab alone
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The same imAE data were public in the 2022 primary paper and the 2023 registry posting, which I could not quote verbatim; a checker may redate this entry to 2022.
safety.judgement: Strengthens, not a new status: the 2017 import is confirmed in the context's own disease. Pairing mine. Grade 3/4 TEAEs were lower on durvalumab (37.1%) than sorafenib (52.4%) in HIMALAYA, so no unpredicted harm appeared in HCC.
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey 4-week and 13-week GLP repeat-dose toxicology of durvalumab (up to 200/100 mg/kg/week)
safety.note: HIMALAYA HCC patients: immune-mediated AEs in 16.5% on durvalumab alone (35.8% with STRIDE), mostly low grade, within three months of starting.
safety.short: HCC patients showed the predicted irAEs
safety.quote: imAEs occurred in 139/388 (35.8%) and 64/388 (16.5%) participants with STRIDE and durvalumab, respectively; most were low grade.
safety.reason: Monkey irAE prediction held in HCC
